statistical_tests.test_name: Chi-Square Test of Independence (Contract Type vs Churn)

hypothesis.H0: Customer churn is independent of contract type (Monthly, Annual, Multi-year).
hypothesis.H1: Customer churn is significantly dependent on contract type.

assumptions: Expected frequencies in each cell are >= 5 (verified: min expected cell count is 21.0).

result.interpretation: Strongly reject H0 (p < 0.0001). Monthly contracts experience 43.94% churn versus 20.71% for Annual and 18.33% for Multi-year (Cramer's V = 0.239).

limitations: Observational study: correlation does not establish causation.
Self-selection bias: customers committing to multi-year contracts typically possess higher baseline product-fit, larger budgets, and greater organizational commitment prior to signing.

statistical_tests.test_name: Chi-Square Test of Independence (Plan Tier vs Churn)

hypothesis.H0: Customer churn is independent of subscription plan tier (Starter, Growth, Professional, Enterprise).
hypothesis.H1: Customer churn rates differ significantly across plan tiers.

assumptions: Expected frequency >= 5 per cell (verified: min expected count is 31.2).

result.interpretation: Reject H0 (p < 0.001). Enterprise plan churn is only 12.36% compared to Starter plan churn of 40.92%.

limitations: Confounding organizational variables: Enterprise customers receive dedicated customer success managers, higher SLA guarantees, and enterprise onboarding, which directly alter retention dynamics independent of software tier.

statistical_tests.test_name: Mann-Whitney U Test (Engagement Total Sessions vs Churn)

hypothesis.H0: The distribution of total session engagement is identical between active and churned customers.
hypothesis.H1: The distribution of total session engagement differs significantly between active and churned customers.

assumptions: Non-parametric distribution (total sessions are right-skewed and non-normal).

result.interpretation: Statistically significant difference (p < 0.0001). Active customers average 541.9 total sessions versus 302.0 sessions for churned accounts.

limitations: Reverse causality / lagging indicator: Decreasing login volume is often a symptom of pre-churn disengagement rather than the root cause of cancellation.
Survivor exposure bias: Customers who stay longer naturally accumulate more sessions over time.

statistical_tests.test_name: Welch's Two-Sample t-Test & Mann-Whitney U (CSAT vs Churn)

hypothesis.H0: Mean customer satisfaction score (CSAT) is identical between active and churned customers who filed support tickets.
hypothesis.H1: Mean CSAT score is significantly lower among churned customers compared to active customers.

statistical_tests.test: Welch's Two-Sample t-Test (Unequal Variances) & Non-Parametric Mann-Whitney U
assumptions: Does not assume equal variances between groups (Welch's formulation).
Samples conditioned on filing at least one ticket.

result.interpretation: Highly significant (p < 0.0001, Cohen's d = 1.83). Active ticket submitters had an average CSAT of 3.80 vs 2.17 for churned users.

limitations: Non-reporting bias: 'Silent churners' (dissatisfied users who simply abandon the application without opening a ticket) are omitted from CSAT metrics.
Post-decision rationalization: Users who have already resolved to cancel may retroactively rate recent tickets more harshly.

statistical_tests.test_name: Fisher's Exact & Chi-Square Test (Payment Delinquency vs Churn)

hypothesis.H0: Customer churn is independent of payment failure events.
hypothesis.H1: Customers experiencing failed payment invoices experience significantly higher churn rates.

statistical_tests.test: Fisher's Exact Test & 2x2 Chi-Square with Yates Correction

result.interpretation: Reject H0 (p < 0.0001). Customers experiencing payment failure have an estimated Odds Ratio of inf of churning compared to customers with zero failed invoices.

limitations: Conflation of voluntary vs involuntary churn: Failed payments may represent expired cards (involuntary) or deliberate customer bank-card cancellations intended to discontinue service without interacting with cancellation flows.

statistical_tests.test_name: Chi-Square Test of Independence (Acquisition Channel vs Churn)

hypothesis.H0: Customer churn is independent of marketing acquisition channel.
hypothesis.H1: Customer churn differs significantly across acquisition channels.

assumptions: Categorical channels (Organic Search, Paid Search, Social Media, Referral, Sales Outreach).

result.interpretation: Channel Chi-Square p-value = 0.0000. Referral channels typically display higher retention, whereas paid channels exhibit higher churn.

limitations: Attribution ambiguity: Last-touch attribution models obscure multi-touch customer journeys.
Channel-to-tier confounding: High-intent enterprise buyers typically enter via outbound sales, whereas SMB starters enter via self-serve search or social.

statistical_tests.test_name: Chi-Square Test of Independence (Geography vs Churn)

hypothesis.H0: Customer churn rate is independent of geographic region.
hypothesis.H1: Customer churn rate differs systematically across geographic regions.

limitations: Regional macroeconomic factors, local currency pricing friction, and regional timezone support hours are unmeasured confounders.
